question.explanation:
First, we pull out the factor of $2$ from the denominator:

\begin{align*} \int \dfrac{x+2}{2x-3}\,\textrm d x &=\int \dfrac{x+2}{2\left(x - \dfrac{3}{2}\right)}\,\textrm d x\\[5pt] &=\dfrac{1}{2}\int \dfrac{x+2}{\left(x - \dfrac{3}{2}\right)}\,\textrm d x. \end{align*}

Then, we draw up our synthetic division table to decompose the integrand into its quotient and remainder.

$$ \begin{array}{c|rrr} & x & x^0\\ {\color{red} \dfrac{3}{2}} & 1 & 2\\ & \downarrow & \dfrac{3}{2}\\ \hline & 1 &{\color{blue} \dfrac{7}{2}} \end{array} $$

So from the synthetic division, we get that

\begin{align*} \dfrac{x+2}{\left(x-\dfrac{3}{2}\right)} &= 1 + \dfrac{\left(\dfrac{7}{2} \right)}{\left(x - \dfrac{3}{2}\right)}\\[5pt] &= 1 + \dfrac{7}{2\left(x - \dfrac{3}{2}\right)}\\[5pt] &= 1 + \dfrac{7}{2x - 3}. \end{align*}

Therefore,

\begin{align*} \int \dfrac{x+2}{2x-3}\,\textrm d x &=\dfrac{1}{2} \int\left(1 + \dfrac{7}{2x - 3} \right) \textrm d x \\[5pt] & = \dfrac{1}{2} \left[ \int \textrm{d}x + 7 \int \dfrac{1}{2x - 3} \, \textrm d x \right]\\[5pt] &=\dfrac{1}{2} \left[x + \dfrac{7}{2}\ln|2x - 3| \right] + C \\[5pt] & = \dfrac{x}{2} + \dfrac{7}{4}\ln|2x - 3| + C. \end{align*}

example.title: Integrating a Rational Function Whose Denominator Contains a Leading Coefficient

question.explanation:
We first need to decompose the integrand into its quotient and remainder parts, which we can do using synthetic division.

We draw up a synthetic division table:

$$ \begin{array}{c|rrrr} & x^3 & x^2 & x^1 & x^0\\ {\color{red}3} & 3 & -2 & 0 & -21\\ & \downarrow & 9 & 21 & 63\\ \hline & 3 & 7 & 21 &{\color{blue}{42}} \end{array} $$

So from the synthetic division, we get that \[ \dfrac{3x^3 - 2x^2 - 21}{x-3} = 3x^2 + 7x + 21 + \dfrac{42}{x-3}. \]

Therefore,

\begin{align*} \int \dfrac{3x^3 - 2x^2 - 21}{x-3} \,\textrm{d}x %&= \int \left(3x^2 + 7x + 21 + \dfrac{42}{x-3}\right)\textrm{d}x \\[5pt] &= 3\int x^2 \, \textrm d x + 7\int x \, \textrm{d} x + 21\int \textrm{d}x + 42 \int \dfrac{1}{x-3}\,\textrm d x \\[5pt] & = x^3 + \dfrac{7}{2}x^2 + 21x + 42\ln|x-3| + C. \end{align*}

example.title: Integrating a Rational Function Whose Denominator is Linear

question.explanation:
We first need to decompose the integrand into its quotient and remainder parts, which we can do using synthetic division.

We draw up a synthetic division table:

$$ \begin{array}{c|rrrr} & x^3 & x^2 & x^1 & x^0\\ {\color{red}-1} & 2 & -3 & 0 & 2\\ & \downarrow & -2 & 5 & -5\\ \hline & 2 & -5 & 5 &{\color{blue}{-3}} \end{array} $$

So from the synthetic division, we get that \[ \dfrac{2x^3 - 3x^2 + 2}{x + 1} = 2x^2 - 5x + 5 - \dfrac{3}{x+1}. \]

Therefore,

\begin{align*} \int_{0}^{2} \dfrac{2x^3 - 3x^2 + 2}{x + 1} \,\textrm{d}x &= \int_{0}^{2} \left( 2x^2 - 5x + 5 - \dfrac{3}{x+1} \right)\textrm{d}x \\[5pt] &= 2\int_{0}^{2} x^2 \, \textrm d x - 5\int_{0}^{2} x \, \textrm{d} x + 5\int_{0}^{2} \textrm{d}x - 3 \int_{0}^{2} \dfrac{1}{x+1}\,\textrm d x \\[5pt] & = \dfrac{2}{3}x^3 \, \Big|_{0}^{2} - \dfrac{5}{2}x^2 \, \Big|_{0}^{2} + 5x \, \Big|_{0}^{2} - 3\ln|x+1| \, \Big|_{0}^{2}\\[5pt] & = \dfrac{2}{3}(2^3 - 0^3) - \dfrac{5}{2}(2^2 - 0^2) + 5(2 - 0) - 3(\ln|2+1| - \ln|0+1|)\\[5pt] & = \dfrac{16}{3} - 10 + 10 - 3\ln{3}\\[5pt] & = \dfrac{16}{3} - 3\ln{3}. \end{align*}

example.title: Integrating a Rational Function Whose Denominator is Linear

question.explanation:
We first need to decompose the integrand into its quotient and remainder parts, which we can do using synthetic division.

We draw up a synthetic division table:

$x^3$ $x^2$ $x^1$ $x^0$
$\color{red}3$ $1$ $-1$ $2$ $-3$
$\color{gray}\downarrow$ $3$ $6$ $24$
$1$ $2$ $8$ $21$

So, from the synthetic division, we get that \[ \dfrac{x^3 - x^2 + 2x - 3}{x - 3} = x^2 + 2x + 8 + \dfrac{21}{x-3}. \]

Therefore, \begin{align*} \int_{0}^{1} \dfrac{x^3 - x^2 + 2x - 3}{x - 3}\,\textrm d x &= \int_{0}^{1} \left( x^2 + 2x + 8 + \dfrac{21}{x-3} \right) \, \textrm d x \\[5pt] &= \int_{0}^{1} x^2\,\textrm d x + 2\int_{0}^{1} x\,\textrm d x + 8\int_{0}^{1} \textrm d x + 21\int_{0}^{1} \dfrac{1}{x-3}\,\textrm d x \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{1}{3}x^3 \, \Bigg|_{0}^{1} + x^2 \, \Bigg|_{0}^{1} + 8x\,\Bigg|_{0}^{1} + 21\ln|x-3|\,\Bigg|_{0}^{1} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{1}{3}(1^3 - 0^3) + (1^2 - 0^2) + 8(1-0) + 21(\ln|1-3| - \ln|0-3|) \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{1}{3} + 1 + 8 + 21(\ln 2 - \ln 3) \\[5pt] %&= \dfrac{1}{3} + 9 + 21\ln\left(\dfrac{2}{3}\right) \\[5pt] & = \bbox[4pt, border: 1px solid lightgray]{\dfrac{28}{3}} + 21\ln\left(\,\bbox[4pt, border: 1px solid lightgray]{\dfrac{2}{3}}\,\right). \end{align*}

example.title: Integrating a Rational Function Whose Denominator is Linear

question.explanation:
First, we pull out the factor of $4$ from the denominator: \begin{align*} \int_{0}^{1} \dfrac{9x-2}{4x+1}\,\textrm {d} x &= \int_{0}^{1} \dfrac{9x-2}{4\left(x + 1/4\right)}\,\textrm {d} x \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{1}{4}\int_{0}^{1} \dfrac{9x-2}{\left(x + 1/4\right)}\,\textrm {d} x \end{align*}

Then, we draw up our synthetic division table to decompose the integrand into its quotient and remainder.

$x^1$ $x^0$
$\color{red}-\dfrac{1}{4}$ $9$ $-2$
$\color{gray}\downarrow$ $-\dfrac{9}{4}$
$9$ $-\dfrac{17}{4}$

So, from the synthetic division, we get that \begin{align*} \dfrac{9x-2}{\left(x+1/4\right)} &= 9 - \dfrac{\left({17}/4\right)}{\left(x + 1/4\right)} \\[5pt] &= 9 - \dfrac{17}{4x+1}. \end{align*}

Therefore, \begin{align*} \int_{0}^{1} \dfrac{9x-2}{4x+1}\,\textrm {d} x &= \dfrac{1}{4}\int_{0}^{1} \left(9 - \dfrac{17}{4x+1}\right) \, \textrm {d}x \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{1}{4}\left[9\int_{0}^{1} \textrm {d} x - 17\int_{0}^{1} \dfrac{1}{4x+1}\,\textrm {d} x \right] \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{1}{4}\left[9x - \dfrac{17}{4}\ln|4x+1|\right]_{0}^{1} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{1}{4}\left[9(1-0) - \dfrac{17}{4}\left(\ln|5| - \ln|1|\right)\right] \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{1}{4}\left[9 - \dfrac{17\ln{5}}{4}\right] \\[5pt] &= \bbox[4pt, border: 1px solid lightgray]{\dfrac{9}{4}} - \dfrac{17}{16}\ln\left(\bbox[4pt, border: 1px solid lightgray]{5}\right). \end{align*}
